answers.question: (2) Is there ANY server-visible behaviour change for these figures from the bump alone, before and after the recompose (card state, badges, re-review prompts, publish gating)?
answers.answer:
No, provided prod's figure_review table has no rows in any state. Surface by surface:
(a) Editor card badge: the client reads only fig.effectiveState, which is 'mt-preview' under both versions. The payload exposes only effectiveState.
(b) Re-review prompt: none exists. The card has a badge and two buttons (Approve/Flag) that are always shown whatever the state. No UI compares versions or hashes.
(c) Reader badge in rendered HTML: cnxml-render calls effectiveState(sidecar, blocks, COMPOSER_VERSION). figureReviewAttr adds data-figure-review="mt-preview" for mt-preview and flagged, which is identical under both versions.
(d) Publish gating: none found. A grep for effectiveState and figureReview across tools/lib, scripts, server/services and server/lib finds nothing outside figureReviewService itself. publicationService does not read figure state.
(e) After the recompose: the server never reads composedVersion. Its only use is carrying the value forward in applyApprovedFigureEdits. So the sidecar restamp from '3' to '4' is also invisible to the server. The card image (translatedImageFor) serves whatever SVG is in prod's checkout. Register ㊱ says the recompose changes bytes only, not pixels, but I did not verify that.
Attribution trap: committed published HTML (for example chapters/03/3-1-…html, last touched 2026-07-14) has NO data-figure-review attribute. It predates both the sidecars (added 2026-09-12, f6069bb9) and the badge feature (added 2026-09-04, 108e4975). So the ㉟ re-render WILL add data-figure-review="mt-preview" to sidecar figures. answers.question: (3) What does the approve path write (renderHash, composerVersion) and how would a future approval interact with '4'?
answers.answer:
The POST /figures/:basename/state route does three things in order:
1. ensureFigureRow inserts the row if missing (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING).
2. setState writes to the DB: state, and render_hash = computeRenderHash(resolvedBlocks, COMPOSER_VERSION) for 'approved' or NULL otherwise, plus flag_kind, note, reviewed_by and reviewed_at.
3. applyApprovedFigureEdits reads the existing sidecar first. It carries composedHash and composedVersion forward unchanged, calls getFigure (whose derived state uses the DB row just written), and rewrites the whole sidecar as {version, basename, state: fig.editorialState, renderHash: computeRenderHash(fig.blocks, COMPOSER_VERSION), composedHash (carried), composedVersion (carried), composerVersion: COMPOSER_VERSION, blocks}.
The route then answers with effectiveState. That sidecar write happens for EVERY state transition, flags and explicit mt-preview included, not just approvals.

State machine, from the probe:
(A) Approval made on a server at '3' (the window between merge and deploy): DB render_hash = H3 and sidecar renderHash = H3. editorialState is 'approved' under '3'. effectiveState is still 'mt-preview', because the carried composedHash is the '1'-era hash H1, not H3. After the '4' deploy, editorialState recomputes H4 ≠ H3 and returns 'mt-preview' on the card and in render. The approval is silently demoted. This is the designed effect of the constant (its docstring), not a defect, and nothing tells the editor.
(B) Approval on a server at '4': DB and sidecar get H4 and composerVersion '4'. editorialState is 'approved'. effectiveState stays 'mt-preview' until publish-figure-svg sets composedHash = renderHash (H4) and composedVersion = '4', after which it is 'approved'. figure-run's isStale sees composedHash ≠ renderHash and schedules exactly that recompose.
Key point: for all 34 chemistry sidecars, the approve → still mt-preview → recompose → approved sequence happens under '3' as well. Their stored hash dates from '1', so any approval today already moves renderHash away from composedHash. The bump does not change how this flow works for them; it only moves which version the new hash is computed under.
Pre-existing gap, uncertain whether deliberate: books/*/figure-text/ is NOT in scripts/git-backup.sh PATHSPECS. A sidecar written by an approval on prod stays uncommitted on prod's disk and never reaches main or the local box where figure-run runs. The loop in (B) cannot close without a manual transfer.

answers.question: (4) Must the server be deployed for tools and server to agree, and what happens in the window between merge and deploy?
answers.answer:
For the 37 sidecars with no state key, and with no prod rows, no deploy is needed for anything observable. The server never reads composedVersion, and editorialState returns before it reads the version.
The deploy is still required for correctness, because the server holds the constant at import (a const in a module cached by require) and hashes approvals with it. Until prod runs '4', any approval is hashed under '3' and is demoted on the later deploy (see (3A)).
Inside prod the window is coherent: prod's code AND its sidecars/media change only when deploy.sh runs git pull (the cron never fetches). Until then prod is '3' throughout. The disagreement is between the dev box (tools at '4', figure-run marks all 34 stale) and prod (server at '3'), and it is visible only for an approved figure.
Window hazards:
(i) An approval or flag made on prod in the window is demoted after deploy with no prompt (flags are unaffected).
(ii) That transition leaves an uncommitted sidecar diff on prod's disk, because figure-text is not backed up. deploy.sh stashes it, pulls, then runs stash pop. The bump's recompose rewrites the composedVersion line of every stamped sidecar. A prod approval rewrites the lines on both sides of it (renderHash and composerVersion, plus an inserted state line). That very likely conflicts: stash pop prints a WARNING, the deploy continues, and conflict markers are left in the file. readSidecar then returns null on the malformed JSON, so the figure drops out of the review panel (resolveFigure → null → skipped) and loses its render badge. Inferred, not tested.
(iii) Split within the box during a deploy: git pull (line 73) happens before npm ci and the restart (line 136). In between, a spawned render child (pipelineService.runRender, run from the project root) reads '4' from disk while the running server still has '3'. If npm ci fails, set -euo pipefail aborts before the restart and the split persists. This is harmless for sidecars with no state.
Aside, not affected by the version: the in-process preview (renderService imports cnxml-render and never runs main()) leaves BOOKS_DIR as the relative literal 'books/efnafraedi-2e'. Under a server/ working directory, readSidecar would find nothing and live preview would show no badge. Prose disagrees about prod's WorkingDirectory, so this is uncertain.

A figure that fails anywhere in the recompose chain (artwork not resolved, prepare, drift guards, ring gate, compose, publish) is never stamped. It stays at '3', so the next `--stale` run picks it up again.

answers.question: (2) Exactly which sidecar fields a recompose rewrites, and their new values
answers.answer:
Exactly one field changes, in all 34 files: `"composedVersion": "3"` becomes `"4"`. It is a one-line diff per file, and key order is unchanged.

These do NOT move:
- `composedHash` keeps its value, because it is copied from the unchanged `renderHash`.
- `renderHash` is unchanged.
- `blocks` and `basename`/`version` are unchanged.
- `composerVersion` stays '1' on all 34, and that is correct. `renderHash` was computed under '1' when the sidecar was minted: re-hashing matches under '1' for 34/34 and under '3' or '4' for 0/34. isStale re-hashes under the sidecar's OWN composerVersion (:289), so '1' must stay. Changing it to '4' would make isStale true for ever.

Publish decides whether to write with `composedHash !== renderHash || composedVersion !== COMPOSER_VERSION`. The second clause is true for all 34, so publish writes all 34.

After the stamp, isStale at '4' is false for 34/34, so the recompose converges.

Outside the sidecars, the recompose also rewrites the published `_IS.svg` files in books/efnafraedi-2e/media/. All 34 have a mapping entry and a media file, and all 34 embed woff2 fonts. ⑥b's P7 recorded that every embedded woff2 blob changes in its `head` table on a recompose, because figure-run.js does not pin SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. defaultSpawn merges process.env (:449), so an operator can export it, but the committed bytes were never pinned to any value. Expect about 34 `M` media files even with no composer change. Judge them by pixels or stripped text group, not by bytes. No image-mapping entry is minted, since all 34 are already mapped.

answers.question: (3) Does the rendered HTML of ch03/ch04 change because of the bump itself, independent of media bytes?
answers.answer:
No. The renderer reads sidecar state in one place only: renderFigure calls `figureReviewAttr(effectiveState(sidecar, blocks, COMPOSER_VERSION))`, which emits only `data-figure-review="mt-preview"|"flagged"`, or nothing when approved. No version or hash is ever written into the HTML.

For these 34 the version argument is never read. editorialState returns 'mt-preview' on `!sidecar.state` before any hashing (sidecar.cjs:98), and none of the 37 sidecars has `state`. So the attribute is `mt-preview` at '3' and at '4'.

State never decides which image is shown. The `_IS.svg` src swap happens at inject (applyImageBasenameSwaps, driven only by image-mapping.json), and cnxml-inject.js reads no figure-text sidecar. renderFigure has no track branch, so faithful and mt-preview behave the same.

Don't credit the next re-render's diff (㉟) to the bump (㊱). The committed ch03/ch04 HTML has 0 `data-figure-review` attributes: mt-preview/03 was last committed 2026-09-05, mt-preview/04 2026-09-06, faithful/03 2026-07-14. There is no faithful/04. Across all books, `git grep data-figure-review` in 05-publication finds 0. The ㉟ re-render will therefore ADD `data-figure-review="mt-preview"` to the <figure> of each sidecar figure that renderFigure reaches, whether or not the bump happens. That change comes from the sidecars existing.

answers.question: When and why was composedVersion introduced?
answers.answer: In a8f9a75df (2026-09-07, 'fix(M5 review editorial/F5)', merged in PR #457 at 633f60a94). Before it, isStale re-hashed the blocks under the CURRENT COMPOSER_VERSION and compared the result with the stored renderHash. Nothing could ever satisfy that check: the publisher copies composedHash from the unchanged renderHash, and only an editor's approval rewrites renderHash. So after a bump every figure recomposed on every run, for ever, while reporting VERDICT ok (measured over 4 runs). The fix added a second stamp: composedHash + composedVersion describe the PUBLISHED ARTWORK and are written by the publisher; renderHash + composerVersion describe the TEXT and are written by mint or approval. isStale now also asks `composedVersion !== COMPOSER_VERSION`, and the block re-hash uses the sidecar's OWN composerVersion. The publisher's write guard was widened to `composedHash !== … || composedVersion !== COMPOSER_VERSION`. A missing composedVersion counts as stale. So '1'->'2' was the first bump this mechanism handled.
